question: What is the usual shape for an average fixed cost curve?
solution:
The correct answer is a __**rectangular hyperbola.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• ** Average fixed cost**

 
 
• **The fixed cost that stays the same no matter how many goods and services a company produces are called the average fixed cost (AFC).**
 
• **In a nutshell, the average fixed cost (AFC) is determined by dividing the total fixed cost by the output level and representing the fixed cost per unit.**
 
• **The average fixed cost is just for the short term because no expense is fixed for an extended period of time.**
 
• **The average fixed cost per unit of output lowers as manufacturing units rise.**
 
• **The average cost per unit also rises as the company produces fewer units.**
 
• **AFC = Total fixed cost/Output (Q)**
 
• **The typically fixed-cost AFC curve resembles a rectangle-shaped hyperbola. **It occurs as a result of the fixed cost being divided by rising output.
 
• **As a result, the AFC curve slopes downward and is a rectangular hyperbola,** meaning that **the area beneath the curve is constant throughout.**
 
• **Asymptotes or axes on a rectangular hyperbola are parallel to one another.**
 
• **The conjugate axis and transverse axes have lengths that are identical.**
 
 

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 
• ** **Inverted V-shaped

 
 
• ​The** lateral umbilical ligament sign**, commonly known as the inverted** "V" sign**, is a symptom of pneumoperitoneum that appears as an inverted** "V" shape** in the pelvis on supine **abdominal radiographs**.
 
• The lateral umbilical ligaments are symbolised by free gas. The inferior epigastric vessels are located in the lateral umbilical ligaments in adults as opposed to neonates, who have umbilical arteries.
 
 
 
• ​**Horizontal line**
 
 
• **​**A **straight line that is parallel to the horizon** or the **ground** is referred to as a **horizontal line**. There is **no slope.**
 
• It is a straight line that is drawn from right to left or left to right in the coordinate plane, **parallel to the x-axis**. In other words, a horizontal line is a straight line that has an intercept solely on the y-axis and not on the x-axis.
